Glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis. In the liver excess glucose can be stored as glycogen (see Fig. 2). In the post absorptive state
this glycogen is broken down by phosphorylase to yield G6P that can be hydrolyzed by glucose 6-phosphatase with the resulting glucose being
released into the circulation to maintain blood glucose levels. As liver glycogen becomes depleted blood glucose levels are maintained by the process
